attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: Accurately describes the then-current state. 'Seemingly every' is rhetorical framing of an observation, not a probability hedge on a forecast.

contract.note: The plain reading (a broad wave of major tech firms plus known safety problems at the time) is ordinary and fair. It doesn't demand a literal count, and the target period ending on the post date fits the statement.

evidence.note: Google's Feb 6, 2023 disclosure: Bard, plus plans to bring generative AI into products starting with Search. A company announcement is direct evidence that the announcement happened.
Microsoft's AI-powered Bing and Edge launch with chat and content generation. The page itself is undated, but the Feb 7, 2023 date is well corroborated, including by e3.
CNBC, Feb 27, 2023: Snap's My AI launch, Snap's own warning about the bot's flaws, and documented Bing chatbot incidents. This backs both the adoption part and the trust and safety part.
Reuters, Feb 27, 2023: Meta's new generative AI product group and a Big Tech rush to put the technology into products.

reviews.rationale: Supported. Before 2023-03-06, Google, Microsoft, Snap and Meta all announced generative AI products or plans, and Reuters describes a broader Big Tech rush. Snap's own warning and the Bing incidents show the trust and safety problems were publicly known. Holdouts outside big tech don't defeat the hyperbolic 'seemingly every'.
